election_dates.primarySnippet: § 8-100. Elections; dates of and hours for voting. 1. (a) A primary election shall be held on the fourth Tuesday in June before every general election unless otherwise changed by an act of the legislature.
election_dates.generalSnippet: (c) The general election shall be held annually on the Tuesday next succeeding the first Monday in November.

state_background_check.value: No — New York removes a sitting officeholder convicted of a felony (or of a crime violating their oath of office) from an office they already hold, but no provision found bars someone from becoming a candidate for office in the first place; and the U.S. Constitution's own qualifications for Congress (age, citizenship, residency) can't be added to by any state regardless
state_background_check.snippet: § 30. Creation of vacancies. 1. Every office shall be vacant upon the happening of one of the following events before the expiration of the term thereof: ... e. His or her conviction of a felony, conviction of a crime involving a violation of his or her oath of office, or upon entering a guilty plea in federal court to a felony, or upon entering a guilty plea in federal court to a crime involving a violation of his or her oath of office. Congressional qualifications are set exclusively by the U.S. Constitution, confirmed per https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R41946.html: "the Framers intended the Constitution to be the exclusive source of qualifications for Members of Congress, and that the Framers thereby 'divested' States of any power to add qualifications."

bio_summary.value: I'm Mike LiPetri. Born and raised in Farmingdale, I'm a home grown, hard-working, straight shooting Long Islander. My mom was a nurse and my dad worked for a utility company. I don't come from a political family. I believe that America can be a stronger, smarter, and safer America. I became an attorney to represent the people and be a voice for the citizens only to take it to the next level by defeating a democrat incumbent to win my seat in the New York State Assembly.

employment_record.value: Accountant at Arthur Andersen; law clerk for Thomas Collier Platt Jr. of the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York; commercial litigator at Shearman & Sterling until 1993; attorney of counsel at Harris Beach; consultant for Cablevision and Lazard until 2016; co-chair at Actum in 2023
employment_record.snippet: Suozzi began his career as an accountant at Arthur Andersen before attending law school. He then served as a law clerk for Thomas Collier Platt Jr. of the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York . Following his clerkship, he worked as a commercial litigator at Shearman & Sterling until 1993. [ 15 ] [ 16 ] After being in public office, Suozzi worked in the private sector as an attorney of counsel at Harris Beach and as a consultant for Cablevision and Lazard until 2016. [ 16 ] [ 17 ] Later after leaving Congress, he joined Actum as a co-chair in 2023.

bio_summary.value: Thomas Richard Suozzi [ 2 ] ( / ˈ s w ɒ z i / SWOZ -ee ; born August 31, 1962) is an American politician serving as the U.S. representative for New York's 3rd congressional district since 2024 and previously from 2017 to 2023. A member of the Democratic Party , he was the county executive of Nassau County on Long Island from 2002 to 2009 and served before then as the mayor of Glen Cove for eight years. His district, which is largely suburban, includes northern Nassau County and parts of northeastern Queens . In 2006 , he ran unsuccessfully against Eliot Spitzer for the Democratic nomination for governor of New York . [ 3 ] Suozzi was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 2016 and reelected in 2018 and 2020 . [ 4 ] He retired from Congress to run again for the Democratic gubernatorial nomination in 2022 , losing to incumbent governor Kathy Hochul . [ 5 ]
